author: Michael Larabel
description: For those having Linux systems with multiple swap devices, such as for swap tiering or layered swap handling, a set of patches posted today for the Linux kernel are looking to improve the situation...
title: New Linux Patches Aim To Better Handle Multiple Swap Devices

author: Michael Larabel
description: Following the recent GA of the AWS M9g series as the first instances powered by the new Graviton5 CPUs, I recently ran benchmarks looking at Graviton4 vs. Graviton5 CPU performance. There was very nice generational gains for the new AWS Graviton processors with the shift from Arm Neoverse-V2 to Neoverse-V3 cores and from DDR5-5600 to DDR5-8800 memory, among other improvements. For those wondering how the Graviton5 ARM server processors compare to AMD EPYC and Intel Xeon, here are some additional comparison data points from the Amazon EC2 cloud.
title: Graviton5 Outperforming Intel Xeon Granite Rapids But Falls Short Of AMD EPYC Turin

author: Michael Larabel
description: Alfonso Siciliano, who has been one of the FreeBSD developers leading the effort on adding a KDE-based desktop option to the FreeBSD installer, provided an update on recent work around adding integrating this desktop option...
title: FreeBSD Desktop Installer Option Working Through NVIDIA Driver Handling, Licensing

author: Michael Larabel
description: GNOME developers working on GNOME OS have received funding from Germany's Prototype Fund to work on creating the GNOME OS "Developer Tool Suite" or also tentatively called their "Test Center" to help in testing experimental applications/libraries in a modern Linux computing world with systemd-sysext, Buildstream, and other newer tech...
title: GNOME OS Creating "Test Center" As Its Take On Apple TestFlight For Experiment Software

author: Michael Larabel
description: Stemming from looking at a proposed Linux kernel patch to alter the Linux kernel's system call number handling, veteran Linux kernel developer Thomas Gleixner went down a rabbit hole of the kernel's system call entry handling to make a number of clean-ups and improvements to the code. That rework to the system call entry handling is now expected to land for the Linux 7.3 kernel cycle...
title: Reworked System Call Entry Handling Slated For Linux 7.3

author: Michael Larabel
description: While the Raspberry Pi 5 is already over two and a half years old, one of the missing elements of its support from the mainline Linux kernel has been the IOMMU driver. We are now seeing Raspberry Pi's downstream IOMMU driver being adapted for mainline with hopes of getting it into the upstream kernel...
title: Raspberry Pi 5 IOMMU Driver Being Worked On For The Mainline Linux Kernel

author: Michael Larabel
description: Cloud Hypervisor 53.0 is now available for this open-source, Rust-based VMM focused on cloud workloads and modern security needs. Originally started at Intel, Cloud Hypervisor continues seeing new development these days by Microsoft, Meta, Arm, and other organizations...
title: Cloud Hypervisor 53 Released With Offloaded Snapshot/Restore Daemon
